extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, consumers, stakeholders, and organizations who want to submit comments on CFPB notices
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for members of the public on how to find CFPB notices that request comment and how to submit comments (including where notices are published, acceptable submission channels, and access to closed dockets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of requests open for comment
rubrics_metrics.description: The CFPB requests public comment on a wide variety of topics to inform our work. These requests can include: proposed rules, requests for information, and Paperwork Reduction Act notices that give the public an opportunity to comment on potential information collections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes the kinds of notices where public input is solicited; it signals that comments may be sought for rulemakings, information gathering, and PRA information collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of notices in the Federal Register
rubrics_metrics.description: All these notices will be published in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices announcing opportunities to comment are formally published in the Federal Register, which serves as the official source for open comment periods and notice text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission channels for comments
rubrics_metrics.description: You can submit comments online at Regulations.gov, by email, by mail, and by hand delivery/courier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple submission methods are accepted; specifics (addresses, docket numbers, required subject lines, format requirements) are provided on the individual notice page—see the notice link for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice-specific details and instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: For details, click on the link for the notice on which you’d like to comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each notice page contains the particular instructions and requirements for submitting comments to that docket (e.g., deadlines, docket numbers, formatting, attachments, and any official contact information).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may comment — no expertise required
rubrics_metrics.description: You don’t have to be an expert or a lawyer to give comments. We invite all individuals to share their views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public participation is open to individuals and organizations regardless of professional credentials; substantive value comes from viewpoints and relevant information, not formal qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to closed notices and posted comments
rubrics_metrics.description: You can also access notices with comment periods that have already closed and read comments posted to Regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CFPB provides an archive of closed notices and a way to browse comments received (via Regulations.gov or the CFPB’s closed notices archive), useful for research or seeing prior public input.
